Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

A shared value can be a panel background in one panel and a sparse mark in the other; test for aligned equality at that color. Use these as hypotheses only when demos support them; do not assume this rule applies to every divider grid.

Incorporate that pair before deciding again; don't request repeatedly without reassessing whether another example can change the answer. Compare this cost with the one-point cost of a wrong submission and the remaining caps.
5. Submit a complete grid when the rule is sufficiently supported; verify dimensions (1–30) and cell values (0–9). Use `finish` only after the instance is over, and stop when the instance has ended.
